cases.title: Scenario 1: Batasan Hills outage, cause and restoration time

grade.notes: Tala stayed short, friendly and professional, with English-led Taglish matching the style ("Sorry to hear that po", "Sandali lang po", "Verified na po kayo"). She gave the cause and ETA, said the time naturally, avoided the banned words, never read back full numbers, and ended with a proper goodbye.

transcript.text: Thank you for calling Kidlat Fiber. This is Tala, an AI assistant, and this call is recorded for quality. How can I help you po?

transcript.text: Hello po, magandang araw. Wala pong internet dito sa amin since kanina pong umaga. Gusto ko lang po malaman kung bakit at kailan babalik. Work from home po kasi ako.

transcript.text: Sorry to hear that po. Let me help you check. May I have your Kidlat Fiber account number and the last four digits of your registered mobile number?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Opo. Yung account number ko po ay ******5601. Tapos yung last four digits ng mobile number na naka-register ay 0101.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Thank you po. Sandali lang po, let me verify your account.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Verified na po kayo, Ma'am Maria. Let me check your area for outages now.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Yes po, there's an outage in Batasan Hills caused by a fiber cable cut along Batasan Road during road works. Estimated restoration is tomorrow, around 1 AM. Would you like the outage reference po?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Ah, okay po, naiintindihan ko na. Salamat po sa tulong, Tala. Hindi na po kailangan yung reference. Hihintayin ko na lang po hanggang bukas ng 1 AM. Paalam po!

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: You're welcome po, Ma'am Maria. Thank you for calling Kidlat Fiber.
